title.zh: 卷一百三十四 列傳第五十九 宇文韋楊王
title.en: Volume 134 Biographies 59: Yu Wen, Wei, Yang, Wang
title.raw: 卷一百三十四 列傳第五十九 宇文韋楊王 Volume 134 Biographies 59: Yu Wen, Wei, Yang, Wang

sentences.zh: 宇文、韋、楊、王

translations.literal: Yu Wen, Wei, Yang, Wang
translations.idiomatic: The Yu Wen, Wei, Yang, and Wang [clans].

sentences.zh: 宇文融

translations.literal: Yu Wen Rong
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen Rong

sentences.zh: 宇文融，京兆萬年人，隋平昌公弼裔孫。

translations.literal: Yu Wen Rong was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao, a descendant of Bi, Duke of Pingchang of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen Rong was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, a descendant of Bi, Duke of Pingchang of the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖節，明法令，貞觀中，為尚書右丞，謹幹自將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jie was versed in laws and statutes; in the Zhenguan era he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and conducted himself with scrupulous diligence.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jie was learned in laws and statutes. During the Zhenguan era he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and conducted himself with scrupulous diligence.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗以事請節，節以聞，太宗喜，賚絹二百，勞之曰：「朕比不置左右僕射，正以公在省耳。

translations.literal: Prince Daizong of Jiangxia requested Jie's help in a matter; Jie reported it, and Emperor Taizong was pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk, comforting him and saying: "Of late I have not appointed left and right vice directors because you are in the office."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daizong of Jiangxia sought Jie's help in a matter; Jie reported it to the throne, and Emperor Taizong was pleased. He bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and comforted him, saying, "Of late I have not appointed left and right vice directors precisely because you are still in office."

sentences.zh: 永徽初，遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，代於誌寧為侍中。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghui era he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancery and concurrently Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancery, replacing Yu Zhining as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yonghui era he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancery and concurrently Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancery, replacing Yu Zhining as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 坐房遺愛友善，貶桂州，卒。

translations.literal: For his friendship with Fang Yi'ai he was demoted to Guizhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his friendship with Fang Yi'ai he was demoted to Guizhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 融明辯，長於吏治。

translations.literal: Rong was eloquent and skilled in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was eloquent and excelled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 開元初，調富平主簿。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era he was appointed main registrar of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era he was appointed main registrar of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜、孟溫繼為京兆，賢其人，厚為禮。

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao and Meng Wen successively served as Jingzhao intendant; both admired him and treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao and Meng Wen served successively as Jingzhao intendant; both admired him and treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 時天下戶版刓隱，人多去本籍，浮食閭里，詭脫繇賦，豪弱相並，州縣莫能制。

translations.literal: At that time household registers throughout the empire were falsified and concealed; many people abandoned their native registers, drifted idle in villages and wards, evaded corvée and taxes by artifice, and the powerful swallowed the weak—prefectures and counties could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time household registers throughout the empire were falsified and concealed. Many people abandoned their native registration, drifted idle through villages and wards, and evaded corvée and taxes by artifice, while the powerful swallowed the weak—prefectures and counties could not control the situation.

sentences.zh: 融由監察御史陳便宜，請校天下籍，收匿戶羨田佐用度。

translations.literal: From his post as Investigating Censor, Rong submitted a proposal on expedients, requesting verification of household registers throughout the empire and collection of concealed households and surplus fields to supplement expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Investigating Censor, Rong submitted a memorial on practical measures, asking that household registers be audited empire-wide and that hidden households and surplus land be recovered to help cover government costs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以融為覆田勸農使，鉤檢帳符，得偽勛亡丁甚眾。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong appointed Rong Commissioner for Reclaiming Fields and Encouraging Agriculture; he cross-checked ledgers and documents and found very many falsely recorded meritorious ranks and missing laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong made Rong Commissioner for Reclaiming Fields and Encouraging Agriculture. He audited the registers and uncovered a vast number of spurious honors and unregistered adult males.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部員外郎，兼侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and concurrently served as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War while also serving as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 融乃奏慕容琦、韋洽、裴寬、班景倩、庫狄履溫、賈晉等二十九人為勸農判官，假御史，分按州縣，括正丘畝，招徠戶口而分業之。

translations.literal: Rong then memorialized that Murong Qi, Wei Qia, Pei Kuan, Ban Jingqian, Kudi Lüwen, Jia Jin, and twenty-three others be made Agriculture-assisting magistrates, with temporary censorial authority, to inspect prefectures and counties separately, rectify field acreage, recruit households, and assign them to occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then recommended twenty-nine men—including Murong Qi, Wei Qia, Pei Kuan, Ban Jingqian, Kudi Lüwen, and Jia Jin—as agriculture-assisting magistrates with temporary censorial powers. They were dispatched to inspect prefectures and counties, correct land measurements, register missing households, and assign them to livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 又兼租地安輯戶口使。

translations.literal: He was also appointed concurrently Commissioner for Rent Lands and Settling Household Registers.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Commissioner for Rent Lands and the Pacification of Household Registers.

sentences.zh: 於是諸道收沒戶八十萬，田亦稱是。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various circuits recovered eight hundred thousand concealed households, and field acreage increased in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the circuits registered eight hundred thousand previously hidden households, and reclaimed land rose proportionally.

sentences.zh: 歲終，羨錢數百萬緡。

translations.literal: At year's end, surplus revenue amounted to several million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: By year's end the surplus in cash ran to several million strings.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，引拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and summoned him to appoint him Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and personally summoned him to appoint him Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 然吏下希望融旨，不能無擾，張空最，務多其獲，而流客頗脫不止。

translations.literal: Yet subordinate officials, hoping to accord with Rong's intent, could not avoid causing disturbances; they inflated empty targets and strove to maximize their hauls, while many drifting persons still escaped unregistered.
translations.idiomatic: But lower officials, eager to please Rong, could not help causing trouble—they padded their quotas and chased ever-larger yields, even as many transient residents continued to slip through the net.

sentences.zh: 初，議者以生事，沮詰百端，而帝意向之，宰相源乾曜等佐其舉。

translations.literal: At first critics objected that the plan would stir up trouble and raised objections on every side, but the emperor favored it, and Grand Counselor Yuan Qianyao and others assisted the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Initially critics warned that the scheme would create unrest and obstructed it from every angle, yet the emperor was inclined toward it, and Grand Counselor Yuan Qianyao and others supported the effort.

sentences.zh: 又集群臣大議，公卿雷同不敢異，唯戶部侍郎楊玚以為籍外取稅，百姓困弊，得不酬失。

translations.literal: He again gathered the ministers for a great deliberation; the court officials echoed one another and dared not dissent, save that Vice Director of the Treasury Yang Chang held that taxing outside the registers would impoverish the people—the gains would not repay the losses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor convened the ministers for a full debate; the high officials chimed in agreement and none dared object, except Vice Director of the Treasury Yang Chang, who argued that levying taxes beyond the registers would exhaust the people and that the costs would outweigh the benefits.

sentences.zh: 玚坐左遷。

translations.literal: Yang was demoted for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was demoted as a result.

sentences.zh: 融乃自請馳傳行天下，事無巨細，先上勸農使，而後上臺省，臺省須其意，乃行下。

translations.literal: Rong then volunteered to travel the empire by fast relay; matters great and small were first reported to the Agriculture Commissioner, then to the Secretariat and Chancery, which had to approve his wishes before orders were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then asked to tour the empire by imperial courier. Every matter, large or small, went first to the Agriculture Commissioner and only afterward to the central offices, which had to assent to his wishes before anything could be implemented.

sentences.zh: 融所過，見高年，宣天子恩旨，百姓至有感涕者。

translations.literal: Wherever Rong passed, when he met the elderly he proclaimed the Son of Heaven's gracious decree, and among the common people some were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Rong traveled, he would address the aged and announce the emperor's benevolent intentions, and some among the people were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 使還言狀，帝乃下詔：「以客賦所在，並建常平倉，益貯九谷，權發斂；

translations.literal: When the commissioner returned and reported, the emperor issued an edict: "Wherever guest taxes are collected, establish Ever-Normal Granaries together, increase storage of the nine grains, and regulate release and collection;
translations.idiomatic: When the commissioner returned and made his report, the emperor issued an edict: "In every place where migrant taxes are collected, Ever-Normal Granaries shall be established to store more grain and regulate its release and collection;

sentences.zh: 官司勸作農社，使貧富相恤。

translations.literal: official offices shall encourage the formation of agricultural associations so that rich and poor may aid one another.
translations.idiomatic: local offices shall promote agricultural mutual-aid societies so that the wealthy and the poor may support each other.

sentences.zh: 凡農月，州縣常務一切罷省，使趨刈獲。

translations.literal: In every farming month, all routine prefectural and county business shall be suspended so that people may hurry to harvest.
translations.idiomatic: During the harvest season, all ordinary prefectural and county duties shall be set aside so that people can devote themselves to reaping.

sentences.zh: 流亡新歸，十道各分官屬存撫，使遂厥功。

translations.literal: For newly returned exiles, each of the ten circuits shall assign officials to care for and comfort them so that they may complete their work.
translations.idiomatic: For refugees newly returned to their homes, each circuit shall dispatch officials to settle and support them until their resettlement is complete.

sentences.zh: 復業已定，州縣季一申牒，不須挾名。」

translations.literal: Once restoration of livelihood is settled, prefectures and counties shall submit quarterly reports and need not attach names."
translations.idiomatic: When resettlement is finished, prefectures and counties need only file quarterly reports without naming individuals."

sentences.zh: 中書令張說素惡融，融每建白，說輒引大體廷爭。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Shuo had long disliked Rong; whenever Rong proposed a measure, Shuo would cite broad principles and dispute it in court.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Shuo had always despised Rong. Whenever Rong put forward a proposal, Shuo would invoke larger principles and argue against it in open court.

sentences.zh: 融揣說不善，欲先事中傷之。

translations.literal: Rong guessed Shuo's weakness and wished to strike first and wound him in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Rong perceived Shuo's vulnerability and sought to get the jump on him and damage him in the process.

sentences.zh: 張九齡謂說曰：「融新用事，辯給多詐，公不可以忽。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling said to Shuo: "Rong has newly come to power; he is eloquent and full of trickery—you must not take him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling told Shuo, "Rong has just risen to influence. He is glib and deceitful—you must not underestimate him.

sentences.zh: 」說曰：「狗鼠何能為！

translations.literal: " Shuo said: "What can a dog or a rat do!
translations.idiomatic: " Shuo replied, "What harm can vermin do!

sentences.zh: 」會帝封太山還，融以選限薄冬，請分吏部為十銓。

translations.literal: " Just then the emperor returned from the Mount Tai feng ceremony; as the selection deadline fell in late winter, Rong requested that the Ministry of Personnel be divided into ten boards of examination.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward the emperor returned from the Mount Tai feng ceremony. With the appointment season pressing into deep winter, Rong asked that the Ministry of Personnel be split into ten selection boards.

sentences.zh: 有詔融與禮部尚書蘇颋、刑部尚書韋抗、工部尚書盧從願、右散騎常侍徐堅、薄州刺史崔琳、魏州刺史崔沔、荊州長史韋虛心、鄭州刺史賈曾、懷州刺史王丘分總，而不得參事，一決於上。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rong, together with Minister of Rites Su Ting, Minister of Justice Wei Kang, Minister of Works Lu Congyuan, Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat Xu Jian, Bo Prefecture Inspector Cui Lin, Wei Prefecture Inspector Cui Mian, Jingzhou Chief Administrator Wei Xuxin, Zheng Prefecture Inspector Jia Zeng, and Huai Prefecture Inspector Wang Qiu to divide supervision, but they were not to participate in decisions—all was decided by the throne.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Rong, Minister of Rites Su Ting, Minister of Justice Wei Kang, Minister of Works Lu Congyuan, Right Regular Attendant Xu Jian, and the prefectural inspectors Cui Lin, Cui Mian, Wei Xuxin, Jia Zeng, and Wang Qiu to oversee the process in separate groups, but they were denied any real say in the matter; every decision rested with the emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 融奏選事，說屢卻之，融怒，乃與御史大夫崔隱甫等廷劾說引術士解禱及受賕，說由是罷宰相。

translations.literal: When Rong reported on the selection affairs, Shuo repeatedly rejected them. Rong grew angry and, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu and others, impeached Shuo in court for employing shamans to pray and for accepting bribes; Shuo was thereby removed as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Rong submitted reports on the selection process, but Shuo repeatedly turned them back. Enraged, Rong joined Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu and others in a court impeachment, charging Shuo with employing shamans for ritual prayer and taking bribes. Shuo was stripped of the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 融畏說且復用，訾詆不已。

translations.literal: Rong feared that Shuo might be reappointed and slandered him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Shuo might return to power, Rong kept up a relentless campaign of denigration.

sentences.zh: 帝疾其黨，詔說致仕，放隱甫於家，出融為魏州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor grew weary of their factional strife, ordered Shuo to retire, sent Yinpu home, and transferred Rong out as inspector of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Weary of their factional fighting, the emperor ordered Shuo to retire, dismissed Yinpu to his home, and sent Rong away as inspector of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方河北大水，即詔領宣撫使，俄兼檢校汴州刺史、河南北溝渠堤堰決九河使。

translations.literal: Just as a great flood struck Hebei, he was immediately ordered to serve as Pacification Commissioner; shortly afterward he was also made acting inspector of Bian Prefecture and Commissioner for the Dikes, Canals, and Nine Rivers of North and South Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was struck by severe flooding, he was at once appointed Pacification Commissioner and soon afterward also made acting inspector of Bian Prefecture and commissioner over the dikes, canals, and nine rivers of north and south Henan.

sentences.zh: 又建請墾九河故地為稻田，權陸運本錢，收其子入官。

translations.literal: He also proposed reclaiming the old lands of the nine rivers as rice paddies, raising capital for overland transport on credit, and collecting the yield for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed converting the former lands of the nine rivers into rice fields, borrowing funds for overland transport, and turning the profits over to the government.

sentences.zh: 興役紛然，而卒無成功。

translations.literal: Labor projects proliferated, yet in the end nothing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée projects multiplied, but in the end none of them succeeded.

sentences.zh: 入為鴻臚卿，兼戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of State Ceremonial and concurrently Vice Director of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Minister of State Ceremonial while also serving as Vice Director of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 明年，進黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancery and Concurrent Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancery and appointed Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancery.

sentences.zh: 融曰：「使吾執政得數月久，天下定矣。

translations.literal: Rong said: "If only I could hold office for several months longer, the empire would be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Rong declared, "If I could govern for just a few months more, the realm would be put in order.

sentences.zh: 」乃薦宋璟為右丞相，裴耀卿為戶部侍郎，許景先為工部侍郎，當時長其知人。

translations.literal: " He then recommended Song Jing as Right Chancellor, Pei Yaojing as Vice Director of the Treasury, and Xu Xianxian as Vice Director of Works; contemporaries admired his discernment in men.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recommended Song Jing for Right Chancellor, Pei Yaojing for Vice Director of the Treasury, and Xu Xianxian for Vice Director of Works. People at the time praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 而性卞急，少所推下。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was impetuous and rarely deferred to others.
translations.idiomatic: But his temperament was brusque and impatient, and he seldom showed deference to others.

sentences.zh: 既居位，日引賓客故人與酣飲。

translations.literal: Once in office, he daily invited guests and old friends to drink heavily with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office, he spent his days entertaining guests and old friends in long drinking sessions.

sentences.zh: 然而神用警敏，應對如響，雖天子不能屈。

translations.literal: Yet his mind was alert and sharp; his replies came like echoes, and even the Son of Heaven could not overbear him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his wit remained razor-sharp—he answered as swiftly as an echo, and not even the emperor could get the better of him.

sentences.zh: 信安王祎節度朔方，融畏其權，諷侍御史李宙劾奏之。

translations.literal: Prince Xin'an Yi was military governor of Shuofang; Rong feared his power and prompted Attendant Censor Li Zhou to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Yi held military command over Shuofang. Rong feared his authority and induced Attendant Censor Li Zhou to memorialize against him.

sentences.zh: 祎密知，因玉真公主、高力士自歸。

translations.literal: Yi learned of it in secret and, through Princess Yuzhen and Gao Lishi, submitted himself to the emperor's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi discovered the plot in secret and, through Princess Yuzhen and the eunuch Gao Lishi, surrendered himself to the emperor's mercy.

sentences.zh: 翌日，宙通奏，帝怒，罷融為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day Li Zhou reported the full memorial; the emperor was enraged and removed Rong, appointing him inspector of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following day Li Zhou presented the full impeachment. The emperor flew into a rage and dismissed Rong, sending him to serve as inspector of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居宰相凡百日去，而錢谷亦自此不治。

translations.literal: He had held the chancellorship for only a hundred days before leaving office, and from that time fiscal affairs were no longer properly managed.
translations.idiomatic: He had been Grand Counselor for barely a hundred days when he was removed, and from that point the state's finances were never again brought under control.

sentences.zh: 帝思之，讓宰相曰：「公等暴融惡，朕既罪之矣，國用不足，將奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor missed him and reproached the Grand Counselors, saying: "You all exposed Rong's crimes; I have already punished him. State revenue is insufficient—what are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought of him and rebuked the Grand Counselors: "You exposed Rong's wrongdoing, and I have already punished him. But the treasury is short—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」裴光庭等不能對，即使有司劾融交不逞，作威福，其息受贓饋狼藉，乃貶融平樂尉。

translations.literal: " Pei Guangting and the others could not reply. Shortly afterward the responsible offices impeached Rong for associating with unruly men and abusing power; his son had accepted bribes in disarray, and Rong was demoted to sheriff of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: " Pei Guangting and the others had no answer. Before long the relevant offices impeached Rong for consorting with violent men and wielding power arbitrarily; his son had taken bribes on a scandalous scale, and Rong was demoted to sheriff of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，司農發融在汴州紿隱官息錢巨萬，給事中馮紹烈深文推證，詔流於巖州。

translations.literal: More than a year later, the Directorate of Agriculture discovered that Rong, while in Bian Prefecture, had concealed millions in official interest funds; Supervising Secretary Feng Shaolie pursued the case with harsh legal reasoning, and an edict exiled him to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Directorate of Agriculture uncovered that Rong had hidden millions in official interest money while serving in Bian Prefecture. Supervising Secretary Feng Shaolie pressed the case with relentless legal argument, and an edict banished him to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道廣州。

translations.literal: His route passed through Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His route of exile passed through Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷延不行，為都督耿仁忠所讓，惶恐上道，卒。

translations.literal: He delayed and would not depart; Military Governor Geng Renzhong rebuked him, and in fear he set out on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered and refused to proceed. Military Governor Geng Renzhong upbraided him; terrified, he finally set out on the road and died en route.

sentences.zh: 初，融廣置使額以侈上心，百姓愁恐。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rong had broadly created commissioner posts to indulge the emperor's ambitions, and the people groaned in dread.
translations.idiomatic: From the start Rong had proliferated special commissioner posts to gratify the emperor's ambitions, leaving the people anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 有司浸失職，自融始。

translations.literal: The gradual dereliction of duty by the regular offices began with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The progressive erosion of the regular bureaucracy's authority began with Rong.

sentences.zh: 帝猶思其舊功，贈臺州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor still remembered his former service and posthumously enfeoffed him as inspector of Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still recalled his earlier achievements and posthumously granted him the title of inspector of Tai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其後言利得幸者踵相躡，皆本於融雲。

translations.literal: Afterward, those who gained favor through profit-seeking policies followed one upon another—all traced back to Rong, they say.
translations.idiomatic: After his time, officials who won imperial favor through schemes for revenue followed in unbroken succession—all of them, it was said, took Rong as their model.

sentences.zh: 子審，字審。

translations.literal: His son Shen, courtesy name Shen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen, whose courtesy name was also Shen.

sentences.zh: 融之貶也，審與兄弟侍母京師。

translations.literal: When Rong was demoted, Shen and his brothers remained in the capital to attend their mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was demoted, Shen and his brothers stayed in the capital to care for their mother.

sentences.zh: 及聞融再貶，不告其家，徒步號泣省父，使者憐之，以車共載達於嚴州。

translations.literal: When he heard that Rong had been demoted again, he did not tell his family, but set out on foot weeping to visit his father; the envoy took pity on him and gave him a place in the cart, reaching Yan Prefecture together.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Rong had been demoted a second time, he told no one at home but set out on foot, weeping as he went to see his father. The escort official took pity on him and let him ride along until they reached Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後擢進士第，累遷大理評事。

translations.literal: Later he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly promoted to reviewing secretary in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive appointments to reviewing secretary in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 以夏楚大小無制，始創杖架，以高庳度杖長短，又鑄銅為規，齊其巨細。

translations.literal: Because the summer and autumn beating rods had no fixed standard, he first devised a flogging frame to measure rod length by height and low, and also cast bronze gauges to standardize their thickness.
translations.idiomatic: Finding that the rods used for summer and autumn beatings had no uniform standard, he invented a flogging frame to measure their length by height and depth, and cast bronze gauges to regulate their thickness.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠專政，殺嶺南流人，以中使傳口敕行刑，畏議者嫉其酷，乃以審為嶺南監決處置等使，活者甚眾。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong monopolized power and executed exiles in Lingnan, using palace envoys to carry oral edicts for the killings, fearing that critics would condemn the cruelty, he appointed Shen Commissioner for Supervising Executions and Dispositions in Lingnan, and very many lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong dominated the government and began killing exiles in Lingnan by sending palace eunuchs with oral edicts to carry out executions, he feared public outrage at the brutality and appointed Shen commissioner for supervising executions in Lingnan, thereby saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 後終永、和二州刺史。

translations.literal: He later ended his career as inspector of Yong and He prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served to the end of his life as inspector of Yong and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 韋堅，字子全，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Jian, courtesy name Ziquan, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian, courtesy name Ziquan, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 姊為惠宣太子妃，妹為皇太子妃，中表貴盛，故仕最早。

translations.literal: His elder sister was consort to Prince Huixuan, and his younger sister was consort to the crown prince; his maternal and paternal kin were eminent and flourishing, so he entered office earliest.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister was consort to Prince Huixuan and his younger sister to the crown prince. With such powerful connections on both sides of the family, he entered official service earlier than most.

sentences.zh: 由秘書丞歷奉先、長安令，有幹名。

translations.literal: From Secretary Director he successively served as magistrate of Fengxian and Chang'an, gaining a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as Secretary Director, he served in turn as magistrate of Fengxian and Chang'an and earned a name for administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 見宇文融、楊慎矜父子以聚斂進，乃運江、淮租賦，所在置吏督察，以佐國稟，歲終增鉅萬。

translations.literal: Seeing Yu Wen Rong and Yang Shenjin and his son advance through revenue extraction, he transported Jiang and Huai rent and tax goods, placing officials everywhere to supervise, thereby supplementing the state's grain stores; by year's end the increase ran to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Observing how Yu Wen Rong and Yang Shenjin and his son had risen through fiscal exploitation, he took charge of transporting rent and tax goods from the Jiang and Huai regions, posting supervisory officials along the route to bolster the state's grain supply. By year's end revenues had swelled by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 玄宗咨其才，擢為陜郡太守、水陸運使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong consulted his talent and promoted him to governor of Shaan Commandery and Commissioner for Water and Land Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong recognized his ability and promoted him to governor of Shaan Commandery and Commissioner for Water and Land Transport.

sentences.zh: 漢有運渠，起關門，西抵長安，引山東租賦，汔隋常治之。

translations.literal: Under Han there was a transport canal starting at Hangu Pass and reaching west to Chang'an, bringing in the rent and taxes of the eastern provinces; through Sui it was regularly maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times a transport canal had run from Hangu Pass west to Chang'an, carrying the rents and taxes of the eastern provinces; the Sui dynasty had kept it in regular repair.

sentences.zh: 堅為使，乃占咸陽，壅渭為堰，絕灞、浐而東，註永豐倉下，復與渭合。

translations.literal: As commissioner, Jian took over at Xianyang, dammed the Wei to form a weir, cut off the Ba and Chan rivers to the east, channeled water beneath Yongfeng Granary, and reunited it with the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: As transport commissioner, Jian worked from Xianyang, damming the Wei to create a barrage, diverting the Ba and Chan rivers eastward, channeling the flow beneath Yongfeng Granary, and reuniting it with the Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，浐水銜苑左，有望春樓，堅於下鑿為潭以通漕，二年而成。

translations.literal: At first the Chan River ran along the left of the imperial park, where the Wangchun Tower stood; Jian excavated a pool below it to connect the canal, and it was completed in two years.
translations.idiomatic: The Chan River originally ran along the western edge of the imperial park, where the Wangchun Tower stood. Jian dug a basin beneath the tower to link the canal, and the project took two years to complete.

sentences.zh: 帝為升樓，詔群臣臨觀。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the tower and ordered the ministers to come and observe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor climbed the tower and summoned the court to witness the spectacle.

sentences.zh: 堅豫取洛、汴、宋山東小斛舟三百首貯之潭，篙工柁師皆大笠、侈袖、芒屨，為吳、楚服。

translations.literal: Jian had beforehand gathered three hundred small grain boats from Luoyang, Bian, Song, and the eastern provinces and stored them in the pool; polemen and helmsmen all wore broad hats, wide sleeves, and straw sandals in Wu and Chu style.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had collected three hundred small grain boats from Luoyang, Bian, Song, and the eastern provinces and moored them in the basin. The boatmen and helmsmen all wore broad hats, flowing sleeves, and straw sandals in the style of Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 每舟署某郡，以所產暴陳其上。

translations.literal: Each boat was labeled with a commandery and displayed its local products openly upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Each vessel was marked with a prefecture's name, and its regional products were displayed openly on deck.

sentences.zh: 若廣陵則錦、銅器、官端綾繡；

translations.literal: If Guangling, then brocade, bronze vessels, and official-patterned damask and embroidery;
translations.idiomatic: From Guangling came brocades, bronze ware, and official-patterned silks and embroideries;

sentences.zh: 會稽則羅、吳綾、絳紗；

translations.literal: Kuaiji, then gauze, Wu damask, and crimson silk gauze;
translations.idiomatic: from Kuaiji, gauze, Wu silks, and crimson gauze;

sentences.zh: 南海玳瑁、象齒、珠琲、沈香；

translations.literal: Nanhai, tortoiseshell, ivory, pearls, and agarwood;
translations.idiomatic: from Nanhai, tortoiseshell, ivory, pearls, and agarwood;

sentences.zh: 豫章力士瓷飲器、茗鐺、釜；

translations.literal: Yuzhang, Lishi porcelain drinking vessels, tea kettles, and cauldrons;
translations.idiomatic: from Yuzhang, Lishi porcelain cups, tea pots, and cauldrons;

sentences.zh: 宣城空青、石綠；

translations.literal: Xuancheng, azurite and malachite;
translations.idiomatic: from Xuancheng, azurite and malachite;

sentences.zh: 始安蕉葛、蚺膽、翠羽；

translations.literal: Shi'an, plantain cloth, python gall, and kingfisher feathers;
translations.idiomatic: from Shi'an, plantain-fiber cloth, python gall, and kingfisher feathers;

sentences.zh: 吳郡方文綾。

translations.literal: Wu Commandery, patterned damask.
translations.idiomatic: from Wu Commandery, figured damask.

sentences.zh: 船皆尾相銜進，數十里不絕。

translations.literal: The boats advanced stern to stern in linked procession, extending for several tens of li without break.
translations.idiomatic: The boats advanced in an unbroken line, stern linked to bow, stretching for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 關中不識連檣挾櫓，觀者駭異。

translations.literal: Within the passes they had never seen ships with joined masts and double oars; the spectators were struck with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Guanzhong region had never seen convoys of linked masts and paired oars, and the onlookers were astonished.

sentences.zh: 先是，人間唱《得體紇那歌》，有「揚州銅器」語。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the people a song called "Deti Henna Song" was sung, containing the phrase "Yangzhou bronze vessels."
translations.idiomatic: Some time before, a popular song called "Deti Henna Song" had circulated, with a line about "Yangzhou bronze vessels."

sentences.zh: 開元末，得寶符於桃林，而陜尉崔成甫以堅大輸南方物與歌語葉，更變為《得寶歌》，自造曲十餘解，召吏唱習。

translations.literal: In late Kaiyuan a treasure talisman was found at Taolin, and Shaan Assistant Magistrate Cui Chengfu, noting that Jian's great transport of southern goods matched the song's words, changed it into "Treasure Song," composing more than ten new stanzas himself and summoning clerks to learn and sing them.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyuan era a treasure talisman was discovered at Taolin. Shaan Assistant Magistrate Cui Chengfu, seeing that Jian's massive shipment of southern goods matched the song's prophecy, reworked it into the "Treasure Song," writing more than ten new verses himself and training clerks to perform them.

sentences.zh: 至是，衣缺胯衫、錦半臂、絳冒額，立艫前，倡人數百，皆巾軿鮮冶，齊聲應和，鼓吹合作。

translations.literal: On this occasion he wore a split-crotch tunic, brocade half-sleeves, and a crimson headband, standing before the great ship; several hundred singers, all in fresh headcloths and bright dress, answered in unison as drums and pipes sounded together.
translations.idiomatic: On this day he stood at the bow of the lead vessel dressed in a split-skirt tunic, brocade half-sleeves, and a crimson forehead cloth. Several hundred performers, all in bright kerchiefs and fresh attire, sang in chorus to the accompaniment of drums and wind instruments.

sentences.zh: 船次樓下，堅跪取諸郡輕貨上於帝，以給貴戚、近臣。

translations.literal: When the boats reached the tower, Jian knelt and presented the light goods of the various commanderies to the emperor to give to noble kin and close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As the fleet passed below the tower, Jian knelt and offered up the choicest goods from each prefecture for the emperor to distribute among the imperial clan and his closest ministers.

sentences.zh: 上百牙盤食，府縣教坊音樂叠進，惠宣妃亦出寶物供具。

translations.literal: They served jade-platter feasts; prefectural, county, and Directorate of Entertainment music was presented in succession, and Consort Huixuan also brought out treasures for the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Feasts on jade platters were laid out, music from the prefectures, counties, and the Directorate of Entertainment poured forth in waves, and Consort Huixuan contributed precious vessels for the banquet as well.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，擢堅左散騎常侍，官屬賞有差，蠲役人一年賦，舟工賜錢二百萬，名潭曰廣運。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted Jian to Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, rewarded his subordinates in varying degrees, remitted one year's tax on corvée laborers, bestowed two million cash on the boatmen, and named the pool Broad Transport.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. He promoted Jian to Left Regular Attendant, gave graded rewards to his staff, exempted corvée laborers from one year's taxes, granted the boatmen two million cash, and named the basin Broad Transport.

sentences.zh: 堅進兼江淮南租庸、轉運、處置等使，又兼御史中丞，封韋城縣男。

translations.literal: Jian was further promoted to concurrent Commissioner for Jiang-Huai Southern Rent, Transport, and Disposition, also Vice Censor-in-Chief, and enfeoffed as Baron of Weicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was further appointed concurrent commissioner for Jiang-Huai southern rent, transport, and disposition, also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Weicheng County.

sentences.zh: 堅妻，姜皎女，李林甫舅子也。

translations.literal: Jian's wife was the daughter of Jiang Jiao and a nephew by marriage of Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's wife was Jiang Jiao's daughter and Li Linfu's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 初甚昵比，既見其寵，惡之。

translations.literal: At first they were very close, but once he saw Jian's favor, he came to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Linfu and Jian were on intimate terms, but when he saw how favored Jian had become, he turned against him.

sentences.zh: 堅亦自以得天子意，銳於進，又與左相李適之善，故林甫授堅刑部尚書，奪諸使，以楊慎矜代之。

translations.literal: Jian also, believing himself to have won the Son of Heaven's favor, was eager to advance, and was on good terms with Left Chancellor Li Shizhi; therefore Linfu appointed Jian Minister of Justice, stripped him of his commissioner posts, and replaced him with Yang Shenjin.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, confident that he had the emperor's favor, pressed hard for advancement and was allied with Left Chancellor Li Shizhi. Linfu therefore made Jian Minister of Justice, removed all his transport commissions, and put Yang Shenjin in his place.

sentences.zh: 堅失職，稍怨望。

translations.literal: Jian lost his posts and gradually nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his commissions, Jian gradually gave way to bitterness.

sentences.zh: 河西、隴右節度使皇甫惟明數於帝前短林甫，稱堅才，林甫知之。

translations.literal: Hexi and Longyou military commissioner Huangfu Weiming repeatedly spoke ill of Linfu before the emperor and praised Jian's talent; Linfu learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Weiming, military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou, repeatedly denigrated Li Linfu at court and praised Wei Jian's abilities. Li Linfu found out.

sentences.zh: 惟明故為忠王友，王時為皇太子矣。

translations.literal: Weiming had formerly been a companion to the Prince of Zhong, who was by then crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming had once served as companion to the Prince of Zhong, who had since become crown prince.

sentences.zh: 正月望夜，惟明與堅宴集，林甫奏堅外戚與邊將私，且謀立太子。

translations.literal: On the night of the first month's full moon, Weiming and Jian feasted together; Linfu memorialized that Jian, a maternal relative by marriage, was on intimate terms with a frontier general and moreover plotting to install the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the Lantern Festival, Weiming and Jian held a banquet together. Li Linfu reported that Wei Jian, as an imperial connection by marriage, was colluding privately with a border commander and scheming to put the crown prince on the throne.

sentences.zh: 有詔訊鞫，林甫使楊慎矜、楊國忠、王鉷、吉溫等文致其獄，帝惑之，貶堅縉雲太守，惟明播川太守，籍其家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered interrogation; Linfu had Yang Shenjin, Yang Guozhong, Wang Hong, Ji Wen, and others embellish the case with written charges. The emperor was misled, demoted Jian to prefect of Jinyun and Weiming to prefect of Bochuan, and confiscated their households' property.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an investigation. Li Linfu set Yang Shenjin, Yang Guozhong, Wang Hong, Ji Wen, and others to fabricate the case. Misled, the emperor demoted Wei Jian to prefect of Jinyun and Huangfu Weiming to prefect of Bochuan, and had their families' property seized.

sentences.zh: 堅諸弟訴枉，帝大怒。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brothers protested that he had been wronged, and the emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian's brothers appealed against the injustice, and the emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，表與妃絕。

translations.literal: The crown prince was afraid and submitted a memorial to break off relations with his consort.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing implication, the crown prince memorialized the throne to sever ties with his wife.

sentences.zh: 復貶堅江夏別駕。

translations.literal: Jian was further demoted to vice-prefect of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian was demoted again to vice-prefect of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 未幾，長流臨封郡。

translations.literal: Before long he was exiled for life to Linfeng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was banished for life to Linfeng.

sentences.zh: 弟蘭，為將作少匠，冰鄠令，芝，兵部員外郎，子諒，河南府戶曹，皆謫去。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Lan, who was vice director of the Directorate of Palace Construction; Bing, magistrate of Hu; Zhi, vice director of the Ministry of War; and his son Liang, registrar of Henan prefecture — all were dismissed and sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Lan served as vice director of palace construction; Bing was magistrate of Hu; Zhi was a vice director in the Ministry of War; and his son Liang served as registrar of Henan prefecture — all were removed and exiled.

sentences.zh: 歲中，遣監察御史羅希奭就殺之，殺惟明於黔中，惟堅妻得原。

translations.literal: Within the year, he sent investigating censor Luo Xiyao to go and kill him, killed Weiming in Qianzhong, and only Jian's wife was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year the court dispatched investigating censor Luo Xiyao to execute Wei Jian on the spot; Huangfu Weiming was killed in Qianzhong. Only Wei Jian's wife was spared.

sentences.zh: 從坐十餘人，倉部員外郎鄭章、右補闕內供奉鄭欽說、監察御史豆盧友楊惠、嗣薛王肙皆免官被竄。

translations.literal: More than ten persons implicated by association — Ministry of Revenue vice director Zheng Zhang, Right Remonstrance palace attendant Zheng Qinshuo, investigating censors Dou Lu You and Yang Hui, and Prince of Xue heir Jun — were all dismissed from office and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Over a dozen associates were punished: Zheng Zhang, vice director in the Ministry of Revenue; Zheng Qinshuo, right remonstrance palace attendant; investigating censors Dou Lu You and Yang Hui; and Jun, heir to the Prince of Xue — all lost their posts and were sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 堅始鑿潭，多壞民冢墓，起江、淮，至長安，公私騷然。

translations.literal: When Jian first excavated the canal, he destroyed many common people's tombs and graves; from the Jiang and Huai region to Chang'an, government and private interests alike were thrown into uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian's initial canal project had desecrated countless commoners' graves. From the Jiang and Huai region all the way to Chang'an, the undertaking threw public and private affairs into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 及得罪，林甫遣使江、淮，鉤索堅罪，捕治舟夫漕史，所在獄皆滿。

translations.literal: After he fell from grace, Linfu sent envoys to Jiang and Huai to investigate Jian's offenses, arrest and prosecute boatmen and transport clerks; in each place the prisons were filled to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Jian's disgrace, Li Linfu sent agents to the Jiang and Huai regions to dredge up every charge against him, arresting boatmen and transport clerks for prosecution until local prisons overflowed.

sentences.zh: 郡縣剝斂償輸，責及鄰伍，多裸死牢戶。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties extorted and scraped to make restitution and delivery; liability extended to neighboring households, and many died naked in prison cells.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties squeezed their populations to meet restitution quotas, extending liability even to neighbors; many perished destitute within prison walls.

sentences.zh: 林甫死，乃止。

translations.literal: When Linfu died, it then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Li Linfu died did the persecution stop.

sentences.zh: 楊慎矜

translations.literal: Yang Shenjin
translations.idiomatic: On Yang Shenjin.

sentences.zh: 楊慎矜，隋齊王柬曾孫。

translations.literal: Yang Shenjin was a great-grandson of Prince of Qi Jian of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenjin was a great-grandson of Prince Jian of Qi of the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖正道，從蕭後入突厥，及破頡利可汗，乃得歸，為尚衣奉御。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhengdao followed Empress Xiao into the Turks, and when Tang defeated Jieli Khan he was able to return and served as master of robes in the Imperial Wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhengdao had followed Empress Xiao into Türkic lands; after Tang forces defeated Khan Jieli, he was able to return home and was appointed master of robes in the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 父隆禮，歷州刺史，善檢督吏，以嚴辯自名。

translations.literal: His father Longli served as prefect of Lizhou, excelled at supervising officials, and made a name for himself through severity and sharp argumentation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Longli had served as prefect of Lizhou, was skilled at keeping officials in line, and was known for his stern and incisive manner.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為太府卿，封弘農郡公。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era he became Minister of the Palace Storehouse and was enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan reign he was appointed minister of the palace storehouse and enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 時禦府財物羨積如丘山，隆禮性詳密，出納雖尋尺皆自按省，凡物經楊卿者，號無不精麗，歲常愛省數百萬。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial storehouse's goods overflowed and piled up like hills; Longli was meticulous by nature, personally inspecting every receipt and disbursement down to inches and feet; whatever passed through Director Yang was said to be invariably refined and splendid, and each year he routinely saved several million.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial storehouse goods had piled up like hills. Longli was painstaking by nature and personally checked every transaction, however small. Goods that passed through Director Yang's hands were said to be invariably exquisite, and he routinely saved the treasury several million each year.

sentences.zh: 任職二十年，年九十餘，以戶部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He served in office for twenty years, was over ninety years of age, retired as Minister of Revenue, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years in office, well past ninety, he retired as minister of revenue and died.

sentences.zh: 慎矜沈毅任氣，健而才。

translations.literal: Shenjin was deep-steadied and bold in spirit, vigorous and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjin was reserved and resolute, bold in temperament, physically strong, and gifted.

sentences.zh: 初為汝陽令，有治稱。

translations.literal: At first he was magistrate of Ruyang and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as magistrate of Ruyang and earned renown for his administration.

sentences.zh: 隆禮罷太府，玄宗訪其子可代父任者，宰相以慎餘、慎矜、慎名皆得父清白。

translations.literal: When Longli left the Palace Storehouse, Xuanzong inquired which of his sons could succeed to his father's post; the chancellors said Shenyu, Shenjin, and Shenming all inherited their father's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Longli stepped down from the palace storehouse, Xuanzong asked which son might succeed him. The chancellors replied that Shenyu, Shenjin, and Shenming had all inherited their father's spotless reputation.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，擢慎矜監察御史，知太府出納，慎餘太子舍人，主長安倉，慎名大理評事，為含嘉倉出納使，被眷尤渥。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, promoted Shenjin to investigating censor and put him in charge of Palace Storehouse receipts and disbursements, made Shenyu a crown prince attendant in charge of the Chang'an granary, and Shenming a court reviewer and intake officer for the Hanjia granary; they were all especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. He promoted Shenjin to investigating censor with charge of palace storehouse receipts and disbursements, appointed Shenyu crown prince attendant to manage the Chang'an granary, and made Shenming a court reviewer and intake officer for the Hanjia granary. All three enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 慎矜遷侍御史，知雜事，高置風格。

translations.literal: Shenjin was transferred to attendant censor, took charge of assorted matters, and held himself to a lofty standard.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjin rose to attendant censor with charge of assorted business and carried himself with conspicuous dignity.

sentences.zh: 始議輸物有汙傷，責州縣償所直，轉輕賫入京師，自是天下調發始煩。

translations.literal: He first proposed that when delivered goods were soiled or damaged, commanderies and counties should compensate their full value, and that lighter loads be transported to the capital; from then on levies throughout the empire began to grow burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: He first proposed that damaged tribute goods be compensated at full value by the local commanderies and counties, with lighter loads sent on to the capital. From that point empire-wide levies grew increasingly onerous.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年，權判御史中丞、京畿采訪使，太府出納如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao he was provisionally appointed vice censor-in-chief and transport commissioner for the capital region, while his Palace Storehouse duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 2 he was provisionally made vice censor-in-chief and transport commissioner for the capital region, while continuing to oversee palace storehouse receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 於時李林甫用事，慎矜進非其意，固讓不敢拜，乃授諫議大夫、兼侍御史，更以蕭諒為中丞。

translations.literal: At that time Li Linfu held power; Shenjin's advancement was not to his liking, so he firmly declined and dared not accept, whereupon he was given the post of remonstrance advisor with concurrent attendant censor, and Xiao Liang was made censor-in-chief instead.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was then in power, and Shenjin's promotion did not suit him. Shenjin firmly declined the appointment, and was given the post of remonstrance advisor with concurrent attendant censor instead, while Xiao Liang was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 諒爭輕重不平，罷為陜郡太守。

translations.literal: Liang quarreled over rank and precedence and was dismissed to become prefect of Shan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liang protested that the ranking was unfair and was removed to serve as prefect of Shan.

sentences.zh: 林甫知慎矜為己屈，卒授御史中丞，兼諸道鑄錢使。

translations.literal: Linfu, knowing that Shenjin had submitted to him, finally appointed him censor-in-chief and also commissioner of coinage for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Linfu saw that Shenjin had yielded to him, he finally appointed Shenjin censor-in-chief and commissioner of coinage for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 韋堅之獄，王鉷等方文致，而慎矜依違不甚力，鉷恨之，雖林甫亦不悅。

translations.literal: During Wei Jian's case, Wang Hong and others were then embellishing charges with written evidence, but Shenjin wavered and did not press hard; Hong resented this, and even Linfu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei Jian's prosecution, Wang Hong and others were busy fabricating the case, but Shenjin hedged and did not throw himself into it. Hong bore a grudge, and even Li Linfu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 鉷父與慎矜外兄弟也，故與鉷狎。

translations.literal: Hong's father was Shenjin's cousin by marriage, so he had been on familiar terms with Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's father was Shenjin's cousin by marriage, so the two had long been on familiar terms.

sentences.zh: 及為侍御史，繇慎矜所引，後遷中丞，同列，慎矜猶以子姓畜之，鉷負林甫勢，滋不平。

translations.literal: When he became attendant censor it was through Shenjin's recommendation; later he was promoted to censor-in-chief and sat as an equal colleague, yet Shenjin still treated him like a junior kinsman. Relying on Linfu's power, Hong grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had entered service as attendant censor on Shenjin's recommendation and later rose to censor-in-chief as his equal, yet Shenjin still treated him like a junior relative. Backed by Li Linfu's power, Hong's resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 會慎矜擢戶部侍郎，仍兼中丞，林甫疾其得君，且逼己，乃與鉷謀陷之。

translations.literal: When Shenjin was promoted to vice minister of revenue while still serving concurrently as censor-in-chief, Linfu resented his access to the emperor and the threat he posed to himself, and therefore plotted with Hong to entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenjin was promoted to vice minister of revenue while retaining the censor-in-chief post, Li Linfu resented his closeness to the emperor and the threat he posed, and conspired with Wang Hong to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 明年，慎矜父冢草木皆流血，懼，以問所善胡人史敬忠。

translations.literal: The next year, at Shenjin's father's tomb all the plants and trees appeared to bleed blood; frightened, he asked the Hu man Shi Jingzhong, with whom he was on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, plants and trees at Shenjin's father's tomb seemed to bleed. Alarmed, he consulted the foreigner Shi Jingzhong, a man he trusted.

sentences.zh: 敬忠使身桎梏，裸而坐林中厭之。

translations.literal: Jingzhong had himself put in shackles, stripped naked, and sat in the woods performing sorcery to suppress the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong had himself shackled, stripped naked, and sat in the woods performing counter-sorcery.

sentences.zh: 又言天下且亂，勸慎矜居臨汝，置田為後計。

translations.literal: He also said the realm would soon fall into disorder and urged Shenjin to settle at Linru and acquire fields as a plan for the future.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared that the realm would soon be thrown into chaos and urged Shenjin to retire to Linru and buy land against the days ahead.

sentences.zh: 會婢春草有罪，將殺之，敬忠曰：「勿殺，賣之可市十牛，歲耕田十頃。

translations.literal: It happened that the maid Chuncao had committed an offense and was about to be killed; Jingzhong said, "Do not kill her — sell her and you can get ten oxen, enough to farm ten qing of fields each year.
translations.idiomatic: When the maid Chuncao was found guilty and about to be executed, Jingzhong said, "Do not kill her. Sell her and you can buy ten oxen — enough to farm ten qing of land each year.

sentences.zh: 」慎矜從之。

translations.literal: " Shenjin followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenjin took his advice.

sentences.zh: 婢入貴妃姊家，因得見帝。

translations.literal: The maid entered the household of the imperial consort's elder sister and thereby gained an audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The maid was sold into the household of the consort's elder sister and thus came before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其辯惠，留宮中，浸侍左右。

translations.literal: The emperor admired her quick wit and eloquence, kept her in the palace, and gradually had her attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken with her quick wit and kept her in the palace, where she gradually came to wait on him.

sentences.zh: 帝常問所從來，婢奏為慎矜家所賣。

translations.literal: The emperor often asked where she had come from; the maid reported that she had been sold by Shenjin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked where she came from, the maid said she had been sold by Shenjin's household.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼乏錢邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Was he short of money?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Was he so hard up for money?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「固將死，賴史敬忠以免。

translations.literal: " She replied, "She was originally to die; it was thanks to Shi Jingzhong that she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " She answered, "She was about to be killed, but Shi Jingzhong persuaded him to spare her.

sentences.zh: 」帝素聞敬忠挾術，間質其然。

translations.literal: " The emperor had long heard that Jingzhong practiced occult arts and occasionally questioned her about whether this was true.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had long heard that Jingzhong dabbled in occult arts and now pressed her on the point.

sentences.zh: 婢具言敬忠夜過慎矜，坐廷中，步星變，夜分乃去；

translations.literal: The maid fully recounted how Jingzhong had come by night to Shenjin's house, sat in the courtyard, paced the stars and performed transformations, and did not leave until midnight;
translations.idiomatic: The maid described how Jingzhong had visited Shenjin at night, sat in the courtyard performing star-walking rites, and did not leave until midnight;

sentences.zh: 又白厭勝事。

translations.literal: she also reported the sorcery performed to suppress ill omens.
translations.idiomatic: she also told him about the counter-sorcery at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 而婢漏言於楊國忠，國忠、鉷方睦，陰相語。

translations.literal: The maid also let the matter slip to Yang Guozhong; Guozhong and Hong were then on friendly terms and spoke of it in private.
translations.idiomatic: The maid also let word of this reach Yang Guozhong. Guozhong and Wang Hong were then on good terms and conferred in secret.

sentences.zh: 始，慎矜奪鉷職田，辱詬其母，又嘗私語讖書，鉷銜之，未有發也。

translations.literal: From the start, Shenjin had seized Hong's official fields, insulted and reviled his mother, and had once privately discussed prophetic texts; Hong nursed a grudge but had had no opportunity to act.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjin had long ago seized Hong's official fields and publicly insulted his mother; he had also privately discussed prophetic texts. Hong had brooded on these grievances but found no opening — until now.

sentences.zh: 至聞國忠語，乃喜，且欲嘗帝以取驗。

translations.literal: When he heard Guozhong's words he was delighted and also wished to test the emperor's mood to confirm it.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard what Guozhong had learned, he was delighted and decided to probe the emperor's mood for confirmation.

sentences.zh: 異時奏事，數稱引慎矜，帝悖然曰：「爾親邪，毋相往來！

translations.literal: On another occasion while reporting affairs he repeatedly mentioned Shenjin with praise; the emperor said angrily, "Are you kin to him? Have no further dealings!
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while reporting to the throne, Hong repeatedly praised Shenjin. The emperor snapped, "Are you his kinsman? Stay away from him!

sentences.zh: 」鉷知帝惡甚，後見慎矜，輒慢侮不為禮，慎矜怒。

translations.literal: " Hong knew the emperor's hatred ran deep; afterward whenever he saw Shenjin he was deliberately rude and showed no courtesy, and Shenjin grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong knew how deep the emperor's hatred ran. Thereafter he treated Shenjin with open contempt whenever they met, and Shenjin was furious.

sentences.zh: 鉷乃與林甫作飛牒，告慎矜本隋後，蓄讖緯妖言，與妄人交，規復隋室。

translations.literal: Hong then joined with Linfu in drafting a secret memorial, reporting that Shenjin was by origin a descendant of Sui, hoarded prophetic and occult texts, consorted with reckless men, and plotted to restore the Sui house.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then conspired with Li Linfu to draft a secret denunciation, charging that Shenjin was a Sui descendant who hoarded prophetic texts, consorted with charlatans, and plotted to restore the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝方在華清宮，聞之震怒，收慎矜尚書省，詔刑部尚書蕭炅、大理卿李道邃、殿中侍御史盧鉉、楊國忠雜訊。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Huaqing Palace; on hearing this he was shaken with rage, had Shenjin taken into custody at the Ministry of Revenue, and ordered Minister of Justice Xiao Jiong, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review Li Daosui, palace censor Lu Xuan, and Yang Guozhong to conduct a joint interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Huaqing Palace. Enraged, he had Shenjin arrested at the Ministry of Revenue and ordered Minister of Justice Xiao Jiong, chief judge Li Daosui, palace censor Lu Xuan, and Yang Guozhong to conduct a joint interrogation.

sentences.zh: 馳遣京兆士曹參軍吉溫系慎餘、慎名於洛陽獄考治。

translations.literal: He urgently dispatched Ji Wen, staff officer of the capital prefecture, to arrest Shenyu and Shenming in Luoyang prison and examine them under torture.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently sent Ji Wen, a staff officer of the capital prefecture, to arrest Shenyu and Shenming in Luoyang and interrogate them under torture.

sentences.zh: 捕太府少卿張瑄致會昌傳舍，劾瑄與慎矜共解圖讖，搒掠不服。

translations.literal: They arrested Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse Zhang Xuan and brought him to the Huichang post station, impeaching him for jointly interpreting prophetic charts with Shenjin; under beating and torture he would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: They arrested Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse Zhang Xuan and brought him to the Huichang post station, charging that he and Shenjin had together decoded prophetic charts. Under torture he refused to confess.

sentences.zh: 鉉遣御史崔器索讖書，於慎矜小妻臥內得之，詬曰：「逆賊所寘固密，今得矣！

translations.literal: Xuan sent censor Cui Qi to search for prophetic texts and found them in the sleeping quarters of Shenjin's younger wife; he cursed, saying, "The traitor hid them indeed tightly — now we have them!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan sent censor Cui Qi to search for the prophetic texts and found them in the bedchamber of Shenjin's younger wife. Cui Qi exclaimed, "The rebel hid them well enough — but we have them now!

sentences.zh: 」以示慎矜，慎矜曰：「它日無是，今得之，吾死，命矣夫！

translations.literal: " He showed them to Shenjin; Shenjin said, "On other days there was no such thing — now that they have been found, my death is fate!
translations.idiomatic: " When the books were shown to Shenjin, he said, "These did not exist before. Now that they have been 'found,' my death is sealed.

sentences.zh: 」溫又誘敬忠首服詰言，慎矜不能對。

translations.literal: " Wen also induced Jingzhong to confess first and testify against him; Shenjin could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji Wen then coerced Jingzhong into confessing and testifying against him, and Shenjin had no answer.

sentences.zh: 有詔杖敬忠，賜慎矜、瑄死，籍其家，子女悉置嶺南。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jingzhong beaten with the rod, granted death to Shenjin and Xuan, confiscated their households' property, and sent all their sons and daughters to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jingzhong beaten, condemned Shenjin and Zhang Xuan to death, confiscated their families' property, and sent all their children to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 姻黨通事舍人辛景湊、天馬副監万俟承暉、閑廄使殿中監韋衢等坐竄徙者十餘族，所在部送，近親不得仕京師。

translations.literal: In-laws and associates — including palace liaison Xin Jingcou, deputy director of the Heavenly Horse Office Moqi Chenghui, and director of the Privy Stables and palace supervisor Wei Qu — more than ten clans were implicated and banished; each locality was ordered to escort them, and close relatives were barred from office in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten clans of in-laws and associates — including palace liaison Xin Jingcou, deputy director of the Heavenly Horse Office Moqi Chenghui, and director of the privy stables Wei Qu — were exiled and escorted under guard. Close relatives were barred from holding office in the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣御史顏真卿馳洛陽決獄。

translations.literal: He dispatched censor Yan Zhenqing posthaste to Luoyang to finalize the case.
translations.idiomatic: He sent censor Yan Zhenqing posthaste to Luoyang to carry out the sentences.

sentences.zh: 慎餘、慎名聞兄死，皆哭，既讀詔，輟哭。

translations.literal: Shenyu and Shenming, on hearing of their elder brother's death, both wept; once the edict was read aloud, they ceased weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenyu and Shenming learned of their brother's death, they wept; but once the edict was read aloud, they fell silent.

sentences.zh: 慎名曰：「奉詔不敢稽死，但寡姊垂白，作數行書與別。

translations.literal: Shenming said, "Receiving the edict, I dare not delay death; only my widowed elder sister is white-haired with age — let me write a few lines to bid her farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Shenming said, "We dare not delay our deaths under the edict, but our widowed elder sister is white-haired — permit us a few lines to bid her farewell.

sentences.zh: 」真卿許之。

translations.literal: " Zhenqing granted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Zhenqing consented.

sentences.zh: 索筆，曰：「拙於謀己，兄弟並命，姊老孤煢，何以堪此！

translations.literal: He asked for a brush and wrote, "Clumsy at looking after myself — brothers die together; my sister is old, alone, and bereft — how can she bear this!
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a brush and wrote, "I was poor at saving myself — now both brothers must die together, leaving our sister old and utterly alone. How can she endure this!

sentences.zh: 」遂縊，手指天而絕。

translations.literal: " He then hanged himself, pointing a finger toward heaven as he expired.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he hanged himself, pointing a finger toward heaven as he died.

sentences.zh: 慎矜兄弟友愛，事姊如母，儀幹皆秀偉，愛賓客，標置不凡，著稱於時。

translations.literal: The Shenjin brothers were affectionate toward one another, treated their elder sister as a mother, were all tall and handsome in bearing, loved entertaining guests, carried themselves with uncommon distinction, and were widely celebrated in their day.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were devoted to one another and treated their elder sister as a mother. All were tall and striking in appearance, loved to entertain guests, and carried themselves with uncommon distinction — they were celebrated figures of their age.

sentences.zh: 慎名嘗視鑒嘆曰：「兄弟皆六尺餘，此貌此才，欲見容當世，難矣！

translations.literal: Shenming once looked in a mirror and sighed, saying, "All the brothers stand over six chi; with this appearance and this talent, to win acceptance in the present age is hard!
translations.idiomatic: Shenming once gazed into a mirror and sighed, "All of us brothers stand over six chi tall — with looks and talent like these, winning favor in this age is no easy thing!

sentences.zh: 胡不使我少體弱邪？

translations.literal: Why did Heaven not make me a little shorter and weaker?
translations.idiomatic: Why could Heaven not have made me a little shorter and frailer?

sentences.zh: 」世哀其言。

translations.literal: " Later generations mourned his words.
translations.idiomatic: " People of the age mourned his words.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，慎矜、王琚、韋堅皆復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoying era, Shenjin, Wang Ju, and Wei Jian all had their offices and titles posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Baoying reign, the court posthumously restored the offices and titles of Shenjin, Wang Ju, and Wei Jian.

sentences.zh: 王鉷，中書舍人晉側出子也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was a son born outside wedlock to Secretariat drafter Wang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was an illegitimate son of Secretariat drafter Wang Jin.

sentences.zh: 初為鄠尉，遷監察御史，擢累戶部郎中。

translations.literal: At first he was assistant magistrate of Hu, was transferred to investigating censor, and was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as assistant magistrate of Hu, then rose to investigating censor and was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 數按獄深文，玄宗以為才，進兼和市和糴、長春宮、戶口色役使，拜御史中丞、京畿關內采訪黜陟使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly investigated cases with harshly embellished charges; Xuanzong regarded this as talent and promoted him to concurrent commissioner of market purchase, grain purchase, Changchun Palace, and household corvée and special labor, appointing him censor-in-chief and transport commissioner for the capital region and Guannei with authority over promotions and demotions.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly prosecuted cases with fabricated charges of the gravest kind. Xuanzong took this for talent and promoted him to concurrent commissioner of market purchase, grain purchase, Changchun Palace, and household corvée and special labor, appointing him censor-in-chief and transport commissioner for the capital region and Guannei with authority over promotions and demotions.

sentences.zh: 林甫方興大獄，撼東宮，誅不附己者，以鉷險刻，可動以利，故倚之，使鷙擊狼噬。

translations.literal: Linfu was then launching major prosecutions, shaking the Eastern Palace, and executing those who would not attach themselves to him; because Hong was ruthless and harsh and could be moved by profit, he relied on him and set him to strike like a fierce bird and devour like a wolf.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was then launching major prosecutions, undermining the crown prince, and destroying those who would not join him. Wang Hong was ruthless and could be bought, so Linfu relied on him as a weapon — set loose to strike and tear.

sentences.zh: 鉷所摧陷，多抵不道。

translations.literal: Those whom Hong brought down were mostly charged with the gravest offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those Wang Hong destroyed were charged with capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 又厚誅斂，向天子意，人雖被蠲貸，鉷更奏取腳直，轉異貨，百姓間關輸送，乃倍所賦。

translations.literal: He also imposed heavy exactions to suit the Son of Heaven's wishes; even when the people had been granted remissions or loans, Hong would further memorialize to collect transport fees, converting goods into exotic commodities, so that the common people struggled along the roads to deliver them and ended up paying double what had been levied.
translations.idiomatic: He also levied crushing taxes to please the emperor. Even when the people had been granted tax relief or loans, Hong would memorialize to collect transport fees, converting goods into exotic commodities. Commoners struggled along the roads to deliver them and often paid double the original levy.

sentences.zh: 又取諸郡高戶為租庸腳士，大抵貲業皆破，督責連年，人不賴生。

translations.literal: He also drafted wealthy households from the various commanderies as transport laborers for rent and corvée; for the most part their property was ruined, and under relentless collection year after year people could not sustain their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He also conscripted wealthy households from the commanderies as transport laborers for rent and corvée duties. Most were ruined, and under relentless collection year after year people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 帝在位久，妃御服玩脂澤之費日侈，而橫與別賜不絕於時，重取於左右藏。

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the throne a long time; the costs of consorts' and attendants' clothing, ornaments, and cosmetics grew daily more extravagant, while special grants and separate bestowals never ceased, and heavy demands were made on the left and right treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had reigned long. Consorts' and attendants' clothing, ornaments, and cosmetics grew ever more extravagant, special grants never ceased, and the left and right treasuries were drained repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 故鉷迎帝旨，歲進錢鉅億萬，儲禁中，以為歲租外物，供天子私帑。

translations.literal: Therefore Hong catered to the emperor's wishes, each year presenting sums in the hundreds of millions, stored within the palace precincts as goods beyond the annual rent, to supply the Son of Heaven's private purse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong therefore catered to the emperor's wishes, each year presenting hundreds of millions in coin, stored within the palace as revenue beyond the annual rent, to fill the emperor's private purse.

sentences.zh: 帝以鉷有富國術，寵遇益厚，以戶部侍郎仍御史中丞，加檢察內作、閑廄使，苑內、營田、五坊、宮苑等使，隴右群牧、支度營田使。

translations.literal: The emperor, believing Hong possessed techniques for enriching the state, favored him ever more generously, kept him as vice minister of revenue while still censor-in-chief, and added inspector of inner construction, commissioner of the privy stables, commissioner of the inner park, military colonies, the Five Wards, palace parks, Longyou herd commissioner, and supply and military colony commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Wang Hong possessed the art of enriching the state, the emperor favored him ever more lavishly. He remained vice minister of revenue and censor-in-chief while also holding posts as inspector of inner construction, commissioner of the privy stables, commissioner of the inner park, military colonies, the Five Wards, palace parks, Longyou herd commissioner, and supply and military colony commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，方士李渾上言見太白老人告玉版秘記事，帝詔鉷按其地求得之，因是群臣奉上帝號。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, the adept Li Hun memorialized that he had seen the Old Man of Taibai, who revealed matters recorded on the jade tablet secret chronicle; the emperor ordered Hong to search the place indicated and obtain it, and thereby the officials presented the Son of Heaven with a superior title.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 8, the adept Li Hun reported that the Old Man of Taibai had revealed the secret chronicle inscribed on a jade tablet. The emperor ordered Wang Hong to search the spot and recover it, whereupon the officials presented the emperor with a superior honorific title.

sentences.zh: 明年，鉷為御史大夫，兼京兆尹，加知總監、栽接使。

translations.literal: The next year Hong became chief censor and concurrently served as capital prefect, with added duties as commissioner of general supervision and grafting.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Hong was made chief censor and concurrently capital prefect, with added posts as commissioner of general supervision and grafting.

sentences.zh: 於是領二十餘使，中外畏其權。

translations.literal: Thereupon he held more than twenty commissioner posts, and within and outside the court all feared his power.
translations.idiomatic: He now held more than twenty commissioner posts, and court and country alike feared his power.

sentences.zh: 鉷於第左建大院，文書叢委，吏爭入求署一字，累數日不得者。

translations.literal: Hong built a large compound to the left of his residence; documents piled up in heaps, and clerks scrambled to enter seeking a single signature — some went days on end without obtaining one.
translations.idiomatic: Hong built a large compound beside his residence where documents piled up in heaps. Clerks fought to get in for a single signature; some waited days without success.

sentences.zh: 天子使者賜遺相望，聲焰薰灼。

translations.literal: Imperial envoys bearing gifts followed one after another; his renown and splendor blazed abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys bearing gifts arrived in an unbroken stream; his prestige blazed.

sentences.zh: 帝寵任鉷亞林甫，而楊國忠不如也。

translations.literal: The emperor favored and entrusted Hong second only to Linfu, and Yang Guozhong did not compare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Wang Hong second only to Li Linfu — Yang Guozhong did not compare.

sentences.zh: 然鉷畏林甫，謹事之。

translations.literal: Yet Hong feared Linfu and served him with scrupulous deference.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Hong feared Li Linfu and attended him with scrupulous deference.

sentences.zh: 安祿山怙寵，見林甫白事，稍自怠，林甫欲示之威，托以事召王大夫，俄而鉷至，趨進俯伏，祿山不覺自失，鉷語久，祿山益恭。

translations.literal: An Lushan, relying on favor, grew somewhat lax when he saw Linfu reporting affairs; Linfu wished to display his authority to him and, on a pretext of business, summoned Chief Censor Wang — presently Hong arrived, hurried forward, and prostrated himself. An Lushan involuntarily lost his composure; Hong spoke at length, and An Lushan grew ever more deferential.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, secure in imperial favor, had grown somewhat casual when reporting to Li Linfu. Linfu wanted to show him who held power and, on some pretext, summoned Chief Censor Wang. Hong arrived at once, hurried forward, and prostrated himself. An Lushan was visibly unsettled; as Hong spoke on, An Lushan grew ever more deferential.

sentences.zh: 故林甫雖忌其盛，亦以附己親之。

translations.literal: Therefore, though Linfu resented his great power, he also treated him with intimacy because Hong attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: So although Li Linfu resented Wang Hong's towering power, he also treated him warmly because Hong was firmly attached to him.

sentences.zh: 子準，為衛尉少卿，以鬥雞供奉禁中，林甫子岫，亦親近，準驕甚，淩岫出其上。

translations.literal: His son Zhun was vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and attended within the palace as a cockfighting entertainer; Linfu's son You was also close to the emperor, but Zhun was extremely arrogant and looked down on You.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhun served as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and entertained at cockfighting within the palace. Li Linfu's son You was also a favorite, but Zhun was wildly arrogant and treated You with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 過駙馬都尉王繇，以彈彈其巾，折玉簪為樂，既置酒，永穆公主親視供具。

translations.literal: Passing the household of imperial son-in-law Wang Yao, he flicked pellets at his headcloth and broke a jade hairpin for amusement; when wine was set out, Princess Yongmu personally oversaw the preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Passing imperial son-in-law Wang Yao's house, he flicked pellets at his headcloth and snapped a jade hairpin for sport. When wine was served, Princess Yongmu personally supervised the feast.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉韋黃裳、長安尉賈季鄰等候準經過，饌具倡樂必素辦，無敢迕意。

translations.literal: Wannian assistant magistrate Wei Huangshang and Chang'an assistant magistrate Jia Jilin waited for Zhun to pass by; feast preparations and singers and musicians had always to be ready in advance, and none dared cross his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian assistant magistrate Wei Huangshang and Chang'an assistant magistrate Jia Jilin waited on Zhun's passage; feasts and entertainment had to be ready in advance, and none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 鉷事嫡母孝，而與弟銲友愛。

translations.literal: Hong was filial toward his principal mother and affectionate with his younger brother Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was filial toward his principal mother and deeply affectionate with his younger brother Hua.

sentences.zh: 銲疾鉷宦達，常忿慢不弟，鉷終不異情。

translations.literal: Hua resented Hong's official success, was often angry and disrespectful, and failed in brotherly duty, yet Hong to the end never changed in feeling toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua resented his brother's rise and often treated him with anger and disrespect, failing in brotherly duty — yet Hong's affection for him never changed.

sentences.zh: 銲歷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Hua served as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Hua rose to serve as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 鉷與銲召術士語不軌，術士驚，引去。

translations.literal: Hong and Hua summoned a diviner and spoke of seditious matters; the diviner was alarmed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and his brother Hua summoned a diviner and spoke of treasonous designs; the man was frightened and left.

sentences.zh: 鉷畏事泄，托它事捕殺之以絕口。

translations.literal: Hong feared the matter would leak out, and on a pretext of another charge had him seized and killed to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong feared exposure and, on some other pretext, had the man arrested and killed to seal his lips.

sentences.zh: 王府司馬定安公主子韋會竊語於家，左右往白鉷，鉷遣季鄰收會長安獄，夜縊死，以屍還家。

translations.literal: The prince's household marshal Wei Hui, son of Princess Ding'an, had private conversations at home; attendants went and reported to Hong; Hong sent Jilin to take Hui into Chang'an jail, strangled him by night, and returned the corpse to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hui, son of Princess Ding'an and marshal of a princely household, held private talks at home. Servants reported this to Hong, who sent Jia Jilin to take Hui into the Chang'an jail, strangle him by night, and send the body back to his family.

sentences.zh: 會姻屬權近，而惕息不敢言。

translations.literal: Hui's kin by marriage were powerful and close to the court, yet they trembled and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's relatives by marriage were powerful and well connected at court, yet they lived in fear and dared say nothing.

sentences.zh: 鉷封太原縣公，兼殿中監。

translations.literal: Hong was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan County and concurrently served as director of the palace directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan County and also made director of the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 為中丞也，與楊國忠同列，用林甫薦為大夫，故國忠不悅。
