translations.literal: As censor-in-chief he sat in the same ranks as Yang Guozhong; because he was made chief censor on Li Linfu's recommendation, Guozhong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as censor-in-chief he sat alongside Yang Guozhong, but when Li Linfu's recommendation made him chief censor, Guozhong took offense.

sentences.zh: 銲與邢縡善，縡，鴻臚少卿璹子也，以功名相期，鉷因銲亦交縡。

translations.literal: Hua was friendly with Xing Yi; Yi was the son of vice minister of guest affairs Shuo, and they looked to each other for fame and achievement; through Hua, Hong also befriended Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was close to Xing Yi, the son of vice minister of guest affairs Shuo; the two expected great things of each other, and through Hua, Hong came to know Yi as well.

sentences.zh: 十一載四月，縡與銲謀引右龍武軍萬騎燒都門、誅執政作難。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 11, Yi and Hua plotted to bring the Right Dragon Martial Army's ten-thousand horsemen to burn the capital gate, kill the chief ministers, and raise a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianbao year 11, Yi and Hua plotted to summon the Right Dragon Martial Army's ten-thousand cavalry to burn the capital gate, kill the chief ministers, and launch a revolt.

sentences.zh: 先二日事覺，帝召鉷付告牒。

translations.literal: Two days earlier the plot was exposed; the emperor summoned Hong and handed him the accusatory report.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before, the plot was discovered; the emperor summoned Hong and gave him the denunciation.

sentences.zh: 鉷意銲與縡連，故緩其事，但督兩縣尉捕賊。

translations.literal: Hong believed Hua was connected with Yi, so he slowed the case and merely urged the assistant magistrates of the two counties to capture the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hong thought Hua was implicated with Yi, so he dragged his feet and only pressed the assistant magistrates of the two counties to catch the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賈季鄰逢銲於路，銲謂曰：「我與縡有舊，今反，恐妄相引，君勿受。

translations.literal: Jia Jilin encountered Hua on the road; Hua said: "Yi and I are old acquaintances. Now that he has rebelled, I fear he may falsely implicate me — do not accept that."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jilin met Hua on the road. Hua told him: "Yi and I go back a long way. Now that he has rebelled, he may falsely drag me in — do not believe it."

sentences.zh: 」既至，縡與其黨持弓刃突出格鬥，鉷與國忠繼至，縡黨相語曰：「勿鬥大夫。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Yi and his band burst forth with bows and blades to fight; Hong and Guozhong arrived afterward, and Yi's followers said to one another: "Do not fight the chief censor."
translations.idiomatic: When they got there, Yi and his men rushed out with bows and blades to fight. Hong and Guozhong arrived soon after, and Yi's followers whispered to one another: "Do not fight the chief censor."

sentences.zh: 」或白國忠曰：「賊語陰相謂不可戰。

translations.literal: Someone reported to Guozhong: "The bandits are secretly telling one another not to fight."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Guozhong: "The rebels are whispering among themselves that they must not fight."

sentences.zh: 」會高力士以飛龍小兒甲騎四百至，斬縡，盡禽其黨。

translations.literal: Just then Gao Lishi arrived with four hundred armored cavalry of the Flying Dragon Boys, beheaded Yi, and captured his entire band.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Gao Lishi arrived with four hundred armored cavalry of the Flying Dragon guard, beheaded Yi, and captured all his followers.

sentences.zh: 國忠奏鉷與謀，帝不信，林甫亦為鉷言，故帝原銲不問。

translations.literal: Guozhong memorialized that Hong had plotted with them; the emperor did not believe it, and Linfu also spoke on Hong's behalf, so the emperor pardoned Hua and did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong reported that Hong had joined the plot, but the emperor refused to believe it. Li Linfu spoke up for Hong as well, so the emperor pardoned Hua and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 然欲鉷請銲罪，使國忠諷之，鉷良久曰：「弟為先人所愛，義不欲舍而謀存。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor wished Hong to denounce Hua's crime and had Guozhong hint at this; after a long silence Hong said: "My younger brother was loved by our forebears; in duty I do not wish to abandon him and scheme to save myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still wanted Hong to accuse Hua and had Guozhong drop hints. After a long pause Hong said: "My younger brother was beloved by our ancestors; I cannot in conscience abandon him and plot to save myself."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞頗怒，而陳希烈固爭當以大逆。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he was quite angry, and Chen Xilie firmly argued the charge should be great treason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered when he heard this, and Chen Xilie insisted the crime should be charged as great treason.

sentences.zh: 鉷未知，方上表自解，有詔希烈訊鉷矣，有司不肯通奏。

translations.literal: Hong did not yet know; he was just submitting a memorial in his own defense when an edict had already ordered Chen Xilie to interrogate Hong, and the offices refused to relay his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Hong knew nothing of this and was submitting a memorial to clear himself when an edict had already ordered Chen Xilie to interrogate him; the offices would not even forward his petition.

sentences.zh: 鉷見林甫，林甫曰：「事後矣。

translations.literal: Hong saw Linfu; Linfu said: "It is too late."
translations.idiomatic: Hong went to see Li Linfu, who told him: "It is too late."

sentences.zh: 」俄而銲至，國忠問曰：「大夫與否？

translations.literal: Soon Hua arrived; Guozhong asked: "Was the chief censor involved or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua was brought in shortly afterward, and Guozhong asked: "Was the chief censor part of it or not?"

sentences.zh: 」未及應，侍御史裴冕叱銲曰：「上以大夫故官君五品，君為臣不忠，為弟不誼。

translations.literal: Before he could answer, attendant censor Pei Mian rebuked Hua: "The Son of Heaven, for the chief censor's sake, gave you a fifth-rank post; as a subject you are disloyal, as a brother you are unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: Before Hua could reply, attendant censor Pei Mian shouted at him: "The emperor gave you a fifth-rank post for the chief censor's sake, yet as a subject you are disloyal and as a brother you are faithless."

sentences.zh: 大夫豈與反事乎？

translations.literal: Would the chief censor have joined a rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Would the chief censor ever have joined a rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」國忠愕然曰：「與，固不可隱；

translations.literal: Guozhong started and said: "If he was involved, that surely cannot be concealed;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong started in surprise and said: "If he was involved, that cannot be hidden;

sentences.zh: 不與，不可妄。

translations.literal: if he was not, it must not be falsely alleged."
translations.idiomatic: if he was not, it must not be falsely claimed."

sentences.zh: 」銲乃曰：「兄不與。

translations.literal: Hua then said: "My elder brother was not involved."
translations.idiomatic: Hua then said: "My elder brother had no part in it."

sentences.zh: 」獄具，詔銲杖死，鉷賜死三衛廚。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, an edict ordered Hua beaten to death; Hong was granted death by strangulation in the Three Guard kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was closed, an edict ordered Hua beaten to death; Hong was granted the privilege of death by strangulation in the Three Guard kitchens.

sentences.zh: 冕請國忠，以其屍歸斂葬之。

translations.literal: Pei Mian asked Guozhong to let Hong's corpse be taken home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian asked Guozhong to allow Hong's body to be taken home for proper burial.

sentences.zh: 諸子悉誅，家屬徙遠方。

translations.literal: All his sons were executed and his family was banished to distant places.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons were put to death and his household was exiled to distant regions.

sentences.zh: 有司籍第舍，數日不能遍，至以寶鈿為井幹，引泉激霤，號「自雨亭」，其奢侈類如此。

translations.literal: The offices inventoried his mansion and could not finish in several days; he had used precious inlaid ornaments for well-curb frames and channeled springs to pour down the eaves, calling it the "Self-Raining Pavilion" — his extravagance was of this kind throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inventoried his mansion and could not finish in days. He had used jeweled inlay for well-curb frames and channeled springs to cascade from the eaves in a structure called the "Self-Raining Pavilion" — his luxury was everywhere of this sort.

sentences.zh: 鉷兄錫，見諸弟貴盛，不肯仕，鉷強之，為太子仆。

translations.literal: Hong's elder brother Xi, seeing his younger brothers' splendor and power, refused to serve; Hong forced him and made him palace attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's elder brother Xi, seeing his younger brothers rise to wealth and rank, refused office; Hong pressed him until he accepted the post of palace attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 至是，貶東區尉，死於道，時人傷焉。

translations.literal: At this time he was demoted to assistant magistrate of the Eastern District and died on the road; people of the time mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: Now he was demoted to assistant magistrate of the Eastern District and died on the road; people of the time grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 初，鉷附楊慎矜以貴，已而佐林甫陷慎矜，覆其家。

translations.literal: At first Hong attached himself to Yang Shenjin to rise to wealth and rank; later he assisted Linfu in trapping Shenjin and destroying his house.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Hong had climbed to power by attaching himself to Yang Shenjin; later he helped Li Linfu destroy Shenjin and wipe out his family.

sentences.zh: 凡五年，而鉷亦族矣。

translations.literal: Within five years Hong too was exterminated to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years Hong's entire clan was destroyed as well.

sentences.zh: 盧鉉者，本以御史事韋堅為判官，堅被劾，鉉發其私以結林甫。

translations.literal: Lu Xuan had originally served Wei Jian as case officer while an investigating censor; when Jian was impeached, Xuan exposed his private affairs to ingratiate himself with Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan had first served as investigating censor and case officer under Wei Jian; when Jian was impeached, Xuan exposed his private wrongdoing to win favor with Li Linfu.

sentences.zh: 又善張瑄，及按慎矜，則誣瑄死。

translations.literal: He was also on good terms with Zhang Xuan; when he investigated Shenjin, he falsely charged Xuan to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was also on good terms with Zhang Xuan, but when he investigated Shenjin he framed Xuan and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 至鉷得罪，方為閑廄判官，妄曰：「大夫以牒索馬五百，我不與。

translations.literal: When Hong fell into guilt, Xuan was serving as case officer of the privy stables and falsely said: "The chief censor sent a document demanding five hundred horses and I would not give them."
translations.idiomatic: When Hong fell from power, Xuan was serving as case officer of the privy stables and falsely claimed: "The chief censor sent a document demanding five hundred horses, and I refused."

sentences.zh: 」眾疾其反覆，貶廬江長史。

translations.literal: All despised his fickleness; he was demoted to chief administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone despised his turnabout, and he was demoted to chief administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 它日，見瑄如平生，乃曰：「公何得來此？

translations.literal: One day he saw Xuan as if in ordinary life and said: "My lord, how did you come here?
translations.idiomatic: One day he saw Xuan as if he were still alive and said: "My lord, how did you come here?

sentences.zh: 願假須臾。

translations.literal: Grant me but a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Give me but a moment."

sentences.zh: 」卒死。

translations.literal: He immediately died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：開元中，宇文融始以言利得幸。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Kaiyuan era, Yu Wen Rong first gained favor by speaking of profit.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In the Kaiyuan era, Yu Wen Rong first won the emperor's favor by preaching profit.

sentences.zh: 於時天子見海內完治，偃然有攘卻四夷之心，融度帝方調兵食，故議取隱戶剩田，以中主欲。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven saw the realm wholly ordered and was supinely disposed to drive back the four barbarians; Rong gauged that the emperor was just then preparing troops and provisions, so he proposed taking hidden households and surplus land to hit the emperor's wish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then saw the realm fully at peace and complacently turned his mind to pushing back the four barbarians. Rong judged that he was just then marshaling troops and supplies, so he proposed uncovering hidden households and surplus land to satisfy the ruler's desire.

sentences.zh: 利說一開，天子恨得之晚，不十年而取宰相。

translations.literal: Once the doctrine of profit was opened, the Son of Heaven regretted not having gotten it sooner; within ten years he reached the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Once the gospel of profit was opened, the emperor regretted not having heard it sooner; within ten years Rong had risen to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 雖後得罪，而追恨融才有所未盡也。

translations.literal: Though he later fell into guilt, the emperor still regretted that Rong's talent had not been fully used.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rong later fell from grace, the emperor still regretted that his talent had never been fully exhausted.

sentences.zh: 孟子所謂「上下征利而國危」者，可不信哉！

translations.literal: Was not what Mencius called "when superiors and inferiors contend for profit the state is in peril" worthy of belief!
translations.idiomatic: Was Mencius not right when he said, "When above and below strive for profit, the state is in danger" — can one disbelieve it!

sentences.zh: 天寶以來，外奉軍興，內蠱艷妃，所費愈不貲計。

translations.literal: Since the Tianbao era, outwardly supplying military campaigns and inwardly beguiled by the beautiful consort, expenditures grew beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianbao era onward, the court met rising military costs abroad while the beautiful consort beguiled it at home, and spending grew beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 於是韋堅、楊慎矜、王鉷、楊國忠各以裒刻進，剝下益上，歲進羨緡百億萬為天子私藏，以濟橫賜，而天下經費自如，帝以為能，故重官累使，尊顯烜赫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong each advanced by harsh exaction, stripping the lower to enrich the upper; each year they presented surplus coin in the tens of billions for the Son of Heaven's private store to supply lavish grants, while the realm's regular expenses seemed unchanged; the emperor took this for ability, so he piled offices and commissioner posts upon them, and they stood in towering splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong each rose by ruthless extraction, squeezing the people to enrich the throne. Each year they forwarded tens of billions in surplus coin into the emperor's private hoard to fund lavish gifts, while ordinary state expenses seemed untouched. The emperor took this for competence and heaped offices and commissioner posts on them until they blazed with rank and power.

sentences.zh: 然天下流亡日多於前，有司備員不復事。

translations.literal: Yet refugees in the realm grew daily more numerous than before, and officials held nominal posts and no longer performed their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet refugees in the land grew daily more numerous than before, and officials held empty titles and no longer did their work.

sentences.zh: 而堅等所欲既充，還用權冒以相屠脅，四族皆覆，為天下笑。

translations.literal: When Jian and the others had gotten what they wanted, they still used power and intrigue to destroy one another; all four clans were overthrown and became the world's laughingstock.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jian and the others had gotten what they wanted, they turned power and intrigue against one another; all four families were destroyed and became a laughingstock to the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫民可安而不可擾，利可通而不可竭。

translations.literal: The people may be settled but must not be disturbed; profit may be circulated but must not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The people may be kept at peace but must not be harassed; profit may flow but must not be drained dry.

sentences.zh: 觀數子乃欲擾而竭之，斂怨基亡，則向所謂利者，顧不反哉！

translations.literal: Seeing that these men wished to disturb and exhaust the people, they amassed resentment and laid the foundation for ruin — would not the profit they spoke of turn back upon them!
translations.idiomatic: These men sought to harass the people and drain them dry, amassing resentment and laying the groundwork for ruin — would not the profit they preached turn back upon them!

sentences.zh: 鉷、國忠後出，橫虐最甚，當方毒，天下復思融雲。

translations.literal: Hong and Guozhong came later and their tyranny was most severe; when their cruelty was at its height, the realm again longed for Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Guozhong came later and their oppression was worst of all; when their cruelty peaked, the whole realm again looked back with longing to Yu Wen Rong.
